types.description: A sheet that asks for many separate interchangeable parts degrades the base face to dot eyes without a mouth (sheet-m render, 2026-10-04).
A light grey background comes out mottled and uneven, so the figure cannot be cut out cleanly (base sketches, 2026-10-04).
The words studio and backdrop make the model paint a real photo studio with a paper roll instead of a flat background (known from earlier local renders).
Angles and distances for the limbs, such as 30 degrees or a hand's width, make the model paint an extra arm (known from earlier local renders).
A sentence that lights the scene lays a gradient and glow over the key-colored background (known from earlier local renders).

The three-quarter panel of a turnaround comes out as a second profile, also when the prompt describes it as turned only halfway (ref-12, twice, 2026-10-04). The template asks for front, side and back only; the three-quarter directions come from turning the Blender figure.

The model draws the figure chubby, with a wide round face and a thick body, pulled by the round face of the base sketch and the words big round head (ref-11 and ref-12, 2026-10-04). The spec asks for a slim build and an oval head explicitly.

The edit model keeps the panel layout of its input image: a four-view turnaround as input gave four views although the prompt asked for three (ref-11, 2026-10-04). The base image is a single view, and the cutout refuses a figure count that differs from the template.

A square input image with a single figure and a wide output fills the free space with blotches of greens or other colors, isometric blocks or a second, turned figure (ref-11 to ref-13, 2026-10-04). The maintainer chose ref-11, two isometric views on blotchy green, as the male base; the template asks for exactly those two views, and the cutout takes any green-dominant background.
